n: In July 1830, after Joseph was arrested and tried in Colesville and harassed by mobs, the Lord reminds him that he was called to bring forth the Book of Mormon and has been rescued from his enemies and from Satan.
Joseph’s sins aren’t excused, but the Lord tells him to go and sin no more — mercy paired with accountability.

f.w: go thy way and sin no more

n: Joseph is to magnify his office. After planting his fields, he should go to the branches in Colesville, Fayette, and Manchester, who will support him and be blessed.

f.g: to fulfill one’s calling fully and honorably.

n: If they reject him, they will receive a cursing instead of a blessing.
Joseph should keep praying, recording revelations, and explaining scripture to the Church.
He will be given what to say and write at the very moment it’s needed.

f.w: it shall be given thee in the very moment what thou shalt speak

n: Joseph should devote all his service to Zion, and there he will find strength.
Be patient in trials — there will be many — but endure, for the Lord is with him to the end.

f.w: I am with thee, even unto the end of thy days

n: Joseph won’t have strength for worldly labor, because that isn’t his calling; if he attends to his calling, his needs will be provided.

f.g: ordinary work for earning a living.

n: Oliver is to keep bearing Christ’s name to the world and the Church, never feeling he has said enough.
Oliver’s glory will be in Christ, not himself, whether weak or strong, imprisoned or free.

f.w: In me he shall have glory, and not of himself

n: Oliver should preach always, everywhere, with a voice like a trumpet, and will receive extraordinary strength.

f.w: as with the voice of a trump

n: They should not seek miracles unless commanded, except for casting out devils, healing the sick, and protection against snakes and poisons.

f.w: casting out devils, healing the sick

n: Even these should be done only when requested by those who desire them, as scripture describes.
Where they are rejected, they may shake the dust from their feet as a testimony — a symbolic act from Jesus’ instructions to his apostles.

f.w: casting off the dust of your feet

n: Those who violently attack them will be dealt with by the Lord in his own time.
Those who use the law against Joseph will themselves be cursed by the law.
Joseph should travel without purse, bag, staff, or extra coat; the Church will provide what he needs — the pattern Jesus gave his early disciples.

f.g: a small bag or satchel for food on a journey.

n: Joseph is called to prune the Lord’s vineyard mightily for the last time — an image from Zenos’s allegory of the olive tree. Those he ordains should follow this pattern.

f.w: prune my vineyard with a mighty pruning
